comments.author: @DanielSeacrest
comments.text: That leaked document did say that OpenAI would focus on the multimodal capabilities for GPT-5 (Sound and Image, which would allow for video technically since videos are just a bunch of images with sound). Also, several people within OpenAI (like Sam Altman, I believe he said something like "If they are going to learn autonomy anyway, we might as well teach them how to do it right") have hinted that they are either working to improve model autonomy or working on a new model with autonomy in mind. GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 weren't specifically taught how to be autonomous, its kind of just an ability they gained, but it certainly needs improvement. But just imagine how good autonomous agents could be if that was an actual topic the developers were actively improving (like with more RLHF or finetuning for specifically autonomy), just as how OpenAI may be doing now.

comments.author: @OnigoroshiZero
comments.text:
What people can't understand when they say "but if you don't prompt it or ask it for anything it's useless, it can't do anything on its own", is that these models are inside a box cut off from the rest of the world, and that they do NOT have physical/biological needs to push them in to action. 
If they put GPT-4 in a robot, and they tie some of its functionalities to trigger simulated needs (like battery life = hunger), it will do anything within its capabilities to gain a source of energy.

Humans have such a large list of needs, and even if something is not needed for our survival, it is needed for our mental health or happiness, and every single thing of these can act as a trigger to make us use our collected knowledge to make things. These AI models do NOT have such needs, so they will not go out of their way to do something about them (creating images or music on their own, writing stories, creating games, etc.)
